about.label: About
about.title: What is Dropper
about.desc: “Just drop in a file, and the hassle is handled.” We call these little tools Dropper, and we build and release them as a series. There are three so far. One reads an event document, adds the date and venue to Google Calendar, and writes the WhatsApp/SNS announcement for you. One reads a single sheet with many dates on it — a year planner, for example — and puts them all into your calendar at once. One fills in a tournament entry form with dates of birth, ages and addresses from your club roster (made for Japanese forms). They all work the same way — just drop — so anyone can use them, not only a particular group or sport.
about.desc2: Alongside them there is Attendance. The others take a sheet of paper and get something out of it; this one collects from people instead. The direction is reversed, so it sits on its own shelf. Members pick their name from the roster and tap yes, maybe or no — no app, no sign-up, no login. You can start it from an event you just read, or on its own with no document at all. More tools will be added over time.
privacy.metaDesc: DROPPER's privacy policy. How your data is handled, how the app accesses Google user data, and what is sent when the AI feature is used.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: DROPPER runs in your browser. For Event, Schedule and Entry Forms we never collect, store, or transmit your data. the Attendance tool is the one exception - we hold the attendance data (see its own section).
privacy.s1operator: Operator: 重吉　哲弥 (independent developer)
privacy.s2body: Event, Schedule and Entry Forms run entirely in your browser. Nothing you read is sent to our servers; everything happens inside your own Google account. the Attendance tool is the exception - we hold that data (see its own section below).
privacy.s3title: 3. How we handle Google user data
privacy.s3body: With your permission, DROPPER accesses Google services within the following scopes.
privacy.s3r1b: To add the dates read from your event document or schedule to your own calendar.
privacy.s3r2a:
Access to files this app creates
(drive.file)
privacy.s3r2b: To read the text from your event document or schedule (OCR) and save the document to your own Google Drive.
privacy.s3r3b: To remember which folder your files are saved in, so the same folder is reused across your devices (for example, phone and computer).
privacy.s3n1: All of this data is processed inside your own Google account. We never receive any of it.
privacy.s3n2: drive.file is limited to files this app itself creates. It cannot see the rest of your Google Drive.
privacy.s3n3: Temporary files created for text recognition (OCR) are deleted immediately after the text is read.
privacy.s3n4: These scopes have been reviewed by Google (OAuth verification) and were approved in July 2026.
privacy.s4notice: When the AI feature is used, the event document or schedule file you dropped (PDF or image) is sent as is, through our relay server, to the AI of OpenAI (USA). Whether to use this feature is entirely your choice.
privacy.s4n1: Using AI is opt-in. After you sign in, a dialog asks you to choose "Use AI" or "Do not use AI".
privacy.s4n2: Only if you choose "Use AI" is the file (images are reduced in size) sent through our relay server (Cloudflare Workers) to OpenAI's API. The API key is provided by us; you do not need to enter one. The relay server stores neither the file nor the AI's answer.
privacy.s4n3: To keep our costs within a fixed range, we use OpenAI's free allowance, which is given on the condition that OpenAI may use what is sent to improve its AI. This means OpenAI may use the files you send to improve its AI. Please do not use documents that contain personal information.
privacy.s4n4: Google user data (the text read by Google Drive, and the contents of your Google Calendar or Drive) is never sent to the AI. Only the file you dropped from your own device is sent.
privacy.s4n5: To prevent overuse, the relay server counts only the amount used that day and the number of requests per mark made from shortened, irreversible connection information, and deletes them the next day (up to 20 event files and 10 schedules per person per day).
privacy.s4n6: If you choose "Do not use AI", nothing is sent to the AI.
privacy.s5body: Dropper does not sell, share, or transfer your Google user data to us or to any third party. We never receive Google user data in the first place. The data held for the Attendance tool is likewise never sold or shared with third parties.
privacy.s5n1: The only exception is when you choose "Use AI". Only then is the file you dropped (PDF or image) sent through our relay server to OpenAI's API (section 4). Even then, Google user data is not sent to the AI.
privacy.s5n2: Data sent to OpenAI is handled in accordance with OpenAI's Privacy Policy.
privacy.s5n3: Apart from the above, we never disclose Google user data to any advertiser, analytics provider, or other third party.
privacy.s6body: Dropper uses the following mechanisms to protect your data:
privacy.s7body: For the three tools other than the Attendance tool we store nothing, so we hold none of your Google user data. Only the following information is stored on your device (in the browser's localStorage), and we cannot access it:
privacy.s8body: DROPPER is provided free of charge, and we do not collect or store any payment information. If this policy changes, it will be revised and the change announced.
privacy.s9title: 9. Compliance with the Google API Services User Data Policy
privacy.s9body: DROPPER's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
guide.metaTitle: How to use Event Dropper | Extract text from a PDF or image into Google Calendar
guide.metaDesc: How to use Event Dropper: drop an event document (PDF or image), extract the text from it, and register the date and venue to Google Calendar and the original file to Google Drive automatically. With screenshots.
guide.title:
Event Dropper
User Guide
guide.subtitle: For first-time users
guide.lead: Just drop the event document. The event goes to your Calendar and the file goes to your Drive — in one step. You can also create a WhatsApp/SNS post from the same details.
guide.videoAlt: How-to video for Event Dropper (1:38, Japanese)
guide.videoNote: A how-to video (1:38, in Japanese). It loads the YouTube player only when you press it.
guide.s1body1: Dropper is a web tool that reads an event document (PDF or image), creates the event in your Google Calendar, and saves the file to your Google Drive.
guide.s1body2: No install. Runs in the browser. Reading and saving all happen inside your own Google account. Event Dropper has no server and holds none of your data.
guide.s2body: All you need is a Google account.
guide.st1body: Click "Sign in with Google" and choose your account.
guide.shot2alt: The Sign in with Google button
guide.st1scopeLead: Google will ask for permissions. Dropper requests only these three:
guide.st1sc1: Calendar events — to create the tournament event
guide.st1sc2: Drive files created by Dropper — to save the event document
guide.st1sc3: App configuration data — to remember your settings
guide.shot3alt: Google consent screen listing the three permissions
guide.shot3cap: The consent screen — only three permissions
guide.st2body: Drag and drop the event document PDF or image onto the drop area. You can also click to choose a file.
guide.shot4alt: Dropping an event document PDF onto the drop area
guide.shot4cap: Drag & drop, or click to choose
guide.st3body: The tournament name, date, venue, events and more are read automatically and shown on a card. Always check the results here. Anything wrong can be fixed on the spot.
guide.shot5alt: The result card showing tournament name, date, venue and events
guide.st4body: Click "Register" and everything goes to your Calendar and Drive.
guide.s4r2b: A folder tree <Year> Tournaments / <Month> / Tournament name / in My Drive (e.g. 2026 Tournaments / 09 /), with the event document inside
guide.shot7alt: Google Drive folder structure: year, month, tournament name
guide.s5body: For better reading accuracy you can use AI. It's entirely your choice. The basic reading works without it.
guide.s5sub1body: After signing in, a popup asks whether to use AI. Press "Use AI" and that's it. No API key or sign-up is needed (up to 20 a day per person).
guide.shot8alt: Popup asking whether to use AI
guide.s5note1: 📤 Your event document file is sent through our relay (which stores nothing) to OpenAI's AI. Text read by Google Drive and your calendar contents are never sent.
guide.s5note2: ⚠️ OpenAI may use what you send to improve its AI (the condition for using it free). Do not drop documents with personal information.
guide.s5body2: Your choice is remembered, so the popup won't appear again. To change it, click "AI settings" in the banner at the top of the screen.
guide.s6a1: No. Everything is free to use.
guide.s6a2: Table tennis and several other sports. Pick one from the sport selector at the top of the screen.
guide.s6a3: You can edit the card directly before registering. Some document layouts are harder to read; using AI often helps.
guide.s6q4: How do I delete a registered event?
guide.s6a4: Delete it from Google Calendar and Drive as you normally would. Dropper has no delete function.
guide.s6a5: Event Dropper itself has no server and stores nothing. Only when you use AI mode is your event document file sent to OpenAI through our relay (which stores nothing). See the privacy policy for details.
guide.s7body: For questions or bug reports, contact movie.pingpong@gmail.com. This is a one-person project, so replies may take a while.
privacy.s6n1: All communication takes place over an encrypted connection (HTTPS).
privacy.s6n2: For the three tools other than the Attendance tool we store no data, so nothing of yours sits under our control to be breached. The data held for the Attendance tool is protected on Cloudflare's platform.
privacy.s6n3: Settings (such as whether to use AI) are stored only on your device (in the browser's localStorage). The relay server for the AI feature does not store the files sent or the AI's answers.
privacy.s6n4: All access to Google services takes place under the authentication and authorization of your own Google account.
privacy.s7store1: Whether you chose to use the AI feature
privacy.s7delLead: You can delete this data at any time in the following ways:
privacy.s7del1: Temporary files created for text recognition (OCR) are deleted immediately after reading.
privacy.s7del2: Events created in your Google Calendar and event documents or schedules saved to your Google Drive are managed by you and can be deleted from Google at any time (Dropper has no delete function).
privacy.s7del3: The settings stored on your device can be deleted at any time from your browser settings.
privacy.s7del4: You can revoke Dropper's access to your Google account at any time from your Google Account security settings.
privacy.s10body: Any changes to this policy will be posted on this page. If a change is significant, it will also be announced within the tool.
privacy.s11body: For questions about this policy, please contact movie.pingpong@gmail.com.
privacy.s11lineTitle: 11. About the LINE official account version
privacy.s11lineBody: The LINE official account "Dropper" reads images and PDFs sent in the chat and returns the result. For this feature only, the processing goes through our server (Google Apps Script); in the browser version, only the files sent when you use the AI feature go through our server (section 4). The handling is as follows.
privacy.s11line1: We do not store the images or PDFs you send. They are sent to Google's Gemini API for reading and discarded as soon as processing finishes.
privacy.s11line2: We do not store the extracted content (event name, dates, venue, etc.) either. It is returned to you in the reply and embedded in the link used to add the event to your calendar.
privacy.s11line3: The operator's own API key is used for these requests. Because it runs within the free tier, there is a daily limit per person.
privacy.s11line4: To understand usage, we record only the date and time, the type of item sent, the result, the time taken, and a hashed string derived from your LINE user identifier (first 8 characters only). The original identifier cannot be recovered from this string.
privacy.s11line5: We do not obtain your LINE profile information (display name, profile image, phone number, etc.).
privacy.s11line6: Data sent to the Gemini API is handled according to Google's policies. When used within the free tier, the content sent may be used to improve Google's services.
privacy.attTitle: About the Attendance tool (we do hold this data)
privacy.attBody: Of the tools in this series, only the Attendance tool stores data on our server. Attendance means several people writing from different devices and everyone seeing the same result, which cannot work inside one browser. The other three tools (Event, Schedule, Entry Forms) still run entirely in your browser and we receive nothing.
privacy.att1: What we hold: the group name, the roster (names and gender), event details (title, dates, venue), the replies, and a random id used to recognise a device.
privacy.att2: What we do not hold: email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses. People replying never log in or create an account.
privacy.att3: Where: Cloudflare D1. Servers may be located outside Japan, so data may be transferred abroad.
privacy.att4: Deletion: the organiser can delete the group, roster, events and replies at any time from "Delete this group" in the admin screen. Deletion cannot be undone.
privacy.att5: Retention: data for groups with no activity for a long period may be deleted after notice.
privacy.att6: Who can see what: anyone with the shared URL (the group id) can see the roster names and the counts. Who has not replied is shown only on the organiser’s screen.
privacy.s11analyticsBody: Dropper uses the following tools to understand site usage for the purpose of improving the service. These handle statistical information about site browsing and are unrelated to the contents of your Google Calendar or Drive (Google user data).
privacy.s11a1: Google Analytics: collects statistics such as page views and referrers using cookies. The information collected is anonymized usage statistics and does not identify individuals. Data is handled in accordance with Google's Privacy Policy.
privacy.s11a2: Visitor counter (hits.sh): counts and displays the number of page views. It does not use cookies.
privacy.s11a3: If you do not wish to allow cookies, you can disable them in your browser settings or use the Google Analytics Opt-out Add-on.
privacy.s12body: For questions about this policy, please contact movie.pingpong@gmail.com.
gsched.metaTitle: User guide | Extract a whole schedule into Google Calendar (Schedule Dropper)
gsched.metaDesc: How to use Schedule Dropper. Drop a year planner or a fixture list as a PDF or image, extract the text from it, and add every entry to Google Calendar at once — explained step by step with screenshots. Grid-style calendars supported.
gsched.title:
Schedule Dropper
User guide
gsched.subtitle: For first-time users
gsched.lead: Drop one schedule. Every entry on it is read at once, you check the list, and then they all go into Google Calendar together.
gsched.videoAlt: How-to video for Schedule Dropper (1:18, Japanese)
gsched.videoNote: A how-to video (1:18, in Japanese). It loads the YouTube player only when you press it.
gsched.s1body1: It reads a single sheet packed with dates — a year planner, a fixture list, a season calendar — and adds those entries to your Google Calendar all at once. Instead of typing dozens of entries by hand, you drop the file once.
gsched.s1body2: The difference from Event Dropper, the first tool in the series, is how many entries come off one sheet: Event Dropper takes one entry from one flyer, while Schedule Dropper takes many at once. Note that Schedule Dropper does not write WhatsApp/SNS announcements — that is an Event Dropper feature.
gsched.s2r1b: The owner of the calendar you want the entries added to.
gsched.s2r3b: Free. AI mode also works with no key or sign-up (up to 10 a day per person).
gsched.st1body: Press "Sign in with Google" and choose your account. Calendar and Drive permissions are needed so that entries can be added and the file can be read.
gsched.shot1alt: The opening screen with the "Sign in with Google" button
gsched.shot1cap: Sign in with Google and allow Calendar and Drive access first.
gsched.st2body: Many schedules show dates without a year. If the schedule itself states the year, leave this box blank — it is picked up automatically. If the dates show no year at all, type the year here.
gsched.st2note: If the sheet does not state a year and you leave the box blank, entries can end up on the wrong year. When in doubt, fill it in.
gsched.shot2alt: The reading-mode switch, the year box and the drop area
gsched.shot2cap: Choose how to read it and set the year before you drop the file.
gsched.st3body: Drag the PDF or image onto the area on screen. "Choose a file" works just as well.
gsched.shot3alt: Picking a schedule PDF from the file dialog
gsched.shot3cap: Drag and drop, or pick the file with "Choose a file".
gsched.st4body: Every entry that was read appears in a list. Start, End, Time, Entry and Location can all be edited on the spot. Untick anything you do not want added.
gsched.shot4alt: A list of entries with a tick box on every row
gsched.shot4cap: The number of entries found is shown. Leave only the ones you want ticked.
gsched.st5body: Press "Add all to Google Calendar" and every row that is still ticked goes into your calendar.
gsched.shot5alt: The "Add all to Google Calendar" button below the list
gsched.shot5cap: The ticked rows go into your calendar together.
gsched.s4body: There are two ways to read a schedule. Which one suits you depends on the shape of the sheet, so switch if the result is not what you expected.
gsched.s4r1b: Table-style sheets with one entry per row.
gsched.s4r2b: Calendar grids and heavily designed schedules.
gsched.s4r2c: No setup (up to 10 a day per person).
gsched.s4grid: ⚠️ A calendar grid — the month-by-month layout used by school year planners — cannot be read in normal mode. Once the page is turned into plain text, the link between a date and its entry is lost. Always use AI mode for that shape.
gsched.shot6alt: The "Read it more accurately with AI?" dialog
gsched.shot6cap: Whether to use AI is up to you, and you can change it at any time.
gsched.s4note1: 📤 Your schedule file is sent through our relay (which stores nothing) to OpenAI's AI. Text read by Google Drive is never sent.
gsched.s4note2: ⚠️ OpenAI may use what you send to improve its AI (the condition for using it free). Do not drop documents with personal information.
gsched.s4body2: If entries are missing after a normal-mode read, press "Read again with AI" above the list to run the same file through AI (no key needed).
gsched.s5body: Reading is not perfect. Always look through the list before you add anything.
gsched.s5sub1body: A ⚠ appears on dates that fall outside the year you set. These are never corrected automatically, because some schedules genuinely list such dates. Look at the row and either fix the date or untick it. "Clear ⚠ only" unticks every flagged row in one go.
gsched.s5sub2: With a long list, start small
gsched.s5sub2body: When there are dozens of entries, add just a few first and see how they look in your calendar before adding the rest. "Clear all" lets you start from nothing and tick only what you need.
gsched.s5sub3body: Rows that were added successfully are unticked automatically, so pressing the button again will not put the same entry in twice.
gsched.s5sub4body: "Select all", "Clear all" and "Clear ⚠ only" above the list switch the tick boxes in bulk.
gsched.s6a1: No. Table-style sheets with one entry per row read well, but heavily designed material such as a poster can lose its structure in normal mode and may not be read at all. Use AI mode for calendar grids.
gsched.s6q2: What happens if I leave the year blank?
gsched.s6a2: If the schedule states the year, it is picked up automatically. If it does not, the year cannot be worked out reliably, so typing it in is safer.
gsched.s6a3: You can correct it directly in the list before adding. If there is a lot to fix, reading again with AI often helps.
gsched.s6q4: Will dropping the same schedule twice create duplicates?
gsched.s6a4: Rows that were added are unticked, so pressing the button again will not duplicate them. Reloading the page and adding everything from scratch will, though — check your calendar in that case.
gsched.s6a5: Not in Schedule Dropper. Announcements are a feature of Event Dropper.
gsched.s6a6: Schedule Dropper itself has no server and stores nothing. Only when you use AI mode is your schedule file sent to OpenAI through our relay (which stores nothing). See the privacy policy for details.
gsched.s7body: Because the tools are free, we do not offer one-on-one support. If something is not working, please go through the steps on this page again. When entries are missing, trying AI mode often improves the result.

gattend.metaTitle: User guide | Collect and count attendance with one link (Attendance)
gattend.metaDesc: The user guide for Dropper Attendance. Create a group, paste in your roster and hand out one link. Members need no app, no account and no sign-in - they pick their name from the roster and tap yes, maybe or no. Covers setting up, counting the replies, and sharing them with your officers.
gattend.title:
Attendance
User guide
gattend.subtitle: Start here
gattend.lead: Collect and count replies for a practice or a tournament with a single link. Members need no app, no account and no sign-in. As the organiser you do not need a Google account either, as long as you only want attendance.
gattend.videoPlay: Play the video from the attendance part (0:48, Japanese)
gattend.videoAlt: How-to video for Event Dropper and Attendance (1:38, Japanese)
gattend.videoNote: Plays from the attendance part (0:48) of a how-to video in Japanese. It loads the YouTube player only when you press it.
gattend.s1body1: A web tool that collects and counts replies for practices, tournaments and other events. As the organiser you create a group, put your members in the roster, and hand out one attendance link. Members open it, pick their own name from the roster, and tap yes, maybe or no.
gattend.s1body2: There is one link per group. It does not change when you add another event, so you can pin it to your group chat once and leave it there. You never have to hand out a new link.
gattend.s1body3: Of the four tools in the series, Attendance is the only one where we hold your data. Several people write from different devices and everyone has to see the same result, so it cannot work inside one browser alone. What we hold, and how to delete it, is set out in the privacy policy.
gattend.s1note: This tool is still a preview. Screens and steps may change.
gattend.s2body: Here is everything you need. No Google account, and nothing to install.
gattend.s2r1b: Works on a computer or a phone. Nothing to install.
gattend.s2r2b: Something your members will recognise. You can change it later.
gattend.s2r3b: The names that go in the roster. You can paste them straight out of a spreadsheet. Gender and notes are optional, but gender gives you a breakdown in the count.
gattend.s2r4a: A way to reach your members
gattend.s2r4b: However you hand out the attendance link - a group chat, email, or printed on paper.
gattend.s2key: 🔑 Your only key as the organiser is the admin link. There is no password and no account. Lose that link and nothing can be recovered. Step 2 tells you to save it, and you should.
gattend.s2safe: Members pick a name from the roster. There is no sign-up and no sign-in. The name they pick is remembered on that device, so they do not have to pick again.
gattend.st1body: Open the Attendance admin screen, fill in the group name and your members' names under “Create a group”, and press “Create with this”. Names on their own are enough.
gattend.st1note: A roster in a spreadsheet or a text file can go in all at once with “≡ Paste a list”. One person per line. Separate with a tab or a comma if you are also adding gender and a note.
gattend.st1note2: There is a switch marked “Let members see who answered yes, maybe or no, by name”. Turn it off and members see only the counts, split by gender. Either way you see the names on the admin screen, because you need them to pick a team. You can change it later.
gattend.st2body: Once the group exists, the admin link is shown once. That link is your key, and it is never shown again after you close the screen.
gattend.st2note: ⚠️ Lose the admin link and the roster and the replies are gone for good. We do not store the key itself on our server, so there is nothing for us to send you if you ask. Press “Copy” on the screen and paste it into the URL field of a bookmark, or send it to yourself in a message.
gattend.st2note2: Do not simply bookmark the address bar. The key part may not be included. Always use the “Copy” button on the screen.
gattend.st3body: Add events under “Turn an event into attendance” on the admin screen. “+ Add one by hand” lets you fill in the event name, the date, the entry deadline, the venue and the entries. If you have the event document, you can bring it across from Event Dropper instead (section 6).
gattend.st3note: There are two deadlines. The entry deadline is when you have to enter the tournament. The date your members have to answer by is worked back from it automatically, seven days earlier by default. Replies stop on the answer deadline, and you can change how many days back it sits.
gattend.st4title: Open attendance and hand out the link
gattend.st4body: Press “Open attendance for this event” and replies start coming in. All that is left is to hand the attendance link to your members.
gattend.st4note: There is one link per group, and it never changes. Pin it to your group chat and your members can open it whenever they like. Adding another event does not mean handing out a new link.
gattend.st5body: “All answers” on the admin screen shows the count for each entry and who said yes, maybe or no. Anything a member wrote in their note appears here too.
gattend.st5note: The names of people who have not answered appear only on this admin screen and on the viewing link you give your officers. Members never see them. This is where you find out who to go and ask.
gattend.s4body: Attendance has three links and they do different things. Do not mix up who gets which.
gattend.s4r1c: Edits the roster and the replies, and can delete the whole group. Cannot be recovered if lost.
gattend.s4r2c: Answer, look back at your own answers, see everyone's answers. One per group, and it does not change.
gattend.s4r3c: Read only. Shows who said yes, maybe or no, their notes, and who has not answered. Cannot change anything.
gattend.s4note: When your officers change, press “Reissue” on the admin screen and the old viewing link stops working immediately. Do not give an officer the admin link instead - that one can delete the group.
gattend.s5body: Opening the link they were given puts three tabs along the bottom. Nothing to install, no account to create.
gattend.s5sub1body: The first time, a member picks their own name from the roster and presses “That's me”. That happens once on that device. After that the open events are listed, and they pick yes, maybe or no for each entry and send it. “Note (optional)” is there for things like “running 30 minutes late” or “I can bring two cars”.
gattend.s5sub1note: Answers can be changed as often as they like before the deadline. Tapping the wrong one does no harm.
gattend.s5sub2body: What that member answered, event by event, including the ones they have not answered yet.
gattend.s5sub3body: The count for each entry, split by gender. In groups where the organiser chose to show names, who said yes, maybe or no appears as well. The names of people who have not answered are never shown to members.
gattend.s6body: If you have the event document as a PDF or a photo, read it with Event Dropper first and open attendance from there. The event name, the date, the venue and the entry deadline all carry across.
gattend.s6o1: Read the document with Event Dropper and check the card.
gattend.s6o2: Press “🙋 To the attendance system”. The admin screen opens with the event already brought in.
gattend.s6o3: Press “Open attendance with this”. Replies start, and you are taken back to Event Dropper.
gattend.s6o4: The attendance link is written into the announcement, ready to post to your group chat.
gattend.s6note: On a device you have not used before, open your group first by pasting in the admin link. Press “Remember on this device” and you will not have to paste it again. Do not do this on a shared device - anyone who can use it can then do everything you can.
gattend.s6note2: You do not need a document at all. To use attendance on its own, start from “🙋 Just collect attendance” on the first screen.
gattend.s7q1: Do members have to install an app
gattend.s7a1: No. They open the link in a browser. There is no account to create and nothing to sign in to.
gattend.s7q2: Does the organiser need a Google account
gattend.s7a2: Not for attendance. You are only asked to sign in on the Event Dropper side, when you read a document or add something to your calendar.
gattend.s7a3: We cannot recover it, and we are sorry. The key itself is not stored on our server - if it were, we would be able to read your roster and your replies. Create the group again and hand out the new link.
gattend.s7q4: Can I open the same group on a new phone
gattend.s7a4: Yes, if you saved the admin link: paste it into “Already have a group?” on the admin screen. If you signed in with Google in Event Dropper, your key is kept in your own Google Drive, so signing in on the new device brings it back by itself.
gattend.s7q5: Do I hand out a new link for every event
gattend.s7a5: No. There is one attendance link per group and it never changes.
gattend.s7a6: Under “Group name and members”, write “left” in that person's note and save. They come off the roster.
gattend.s7q7: Can people still answer after the deadline
gattend.s7a7: No. Replies stop on the answer deadline. You can move it with “Change the answer deadline” on the admin screen. The result stays readable afterwards.
gattend.s7q8: How do I delete the data
gattend.s7a8: “Delete this group” on the admin screen removes the roster, the events and every reply. It cannot be undone, and the links you handed out stop opening.
gattend.s7a9: No, and there are no adverts.
gattend.s8body: Because the tools are free, we don't offer one-on-one support. If something isn't working, please go through the steps on this page once more. When a member says the link is not valid, it is almost always because part of the URL was cut off - copy it again from “Attendance link” on the admin screen and send it once more.

tool4.name: Entry Form Dropper
tool4.desc: Drop a blank tournament entry form (Excel), pick the players from your club roster, and it fills in gender, date of birth, age, address and phone number. You can build the roster here too, with addresses filled in from the postcode. Made for Japanese entry forms (the tool is in Japanese only).
picker.t4line: A tournament entry form, filled from your roster
privacy.entTitle: About the Entry Form Dropper (it handles your roster)
privacy.entBody: The Entry Form Dropper handles a tournament entry form and your club roster, which is personal data. Both are processed only inside your browser and are never sent to our server (we have no server, so we cannot receive them). No login is required.
privacy.ent1: What it handles: the entry form (an Excel file) and the roster (names, readings, dates of birth, postcodes, addresses, phone numbers). The filled-in file is also produced on your own device.
privacy.ent2: Nothing is stored: the roster is not saved in your browser. It disappears when you close the page. Please keep the roster as a file of your own.
privacy.ent3: No AI is used: which value goes in which column is decided from the wording of the form’s own headings (“Date of birth”, “Address” and so on).
privacy.ent4: There are only three network requests, and none of them send the names, addresses or phone numbers you entered.
privacy.ent5: (1) Postcode to address and (2) address to postcode: the tool loads postcode data files hosted on this site (Japan Post’s public data). It loads a file; it does not send the postcode or address you typed.
privacy.ent6: (3) Importing the group name, names and sex from the attendance system: only the group ID is sent to the attendance system. The contents of your roster are never sent. What is imported is then handled inside your browser only, as above.
privacy.playBody: The Lantern Museum in the Playground (dropper-tools.com/en/play/spirit.html; renamed from "Monster Dropper" and "Spirit Dropper" in October 2026) is a game that turns museum artworks into spirit cards. Your own photos and files are not used. The artworks were chosen by us from works that The Met, the Art Institute of Chicago, the Cleveland Museum of Art and the National Gallery of Denmark release with their rights waived (CC0), and are hosted on this site. Works showing people's faces or figures, clear writing or logos were left out. The only image you can drop yourself is a life-record image from "1 in 8 billion", used as the key to the last door of the Night Museum (see "What it handles" below). No sign-in is needed.
privacy.play1: What it handles: artwork images are loaded from this site (no connection is made to the museums; a museum's page opens only when you press an artwork's name). Behind the picture on the card, the artwork it came from is drawn darkened, and part of the artwork image is added with light noise; this is saved together with the card. The only images you can drop yourself are the door keys in Light the Night Museum (item 7 below): for doors 2 to 4, an image saved from Silk, NASA's Hubble or TheSkyLive; for the last door, a life-record image from the life simulation "1 in 8 billion" (80億分の1). Any other image is recognised by its layout on your device and turned away without anything being saved. To make a human card from a life-record image, the colours of its life map (age at death, average life expectancy and how happy each year was) are read on your device and used on the card. Life-record images are not sent to any AI.
privacy.play2: What is stored: the cards you make (form, radiance, a small picture and the name of the artwork they came from), the records of bonds and lineage, and a per-device number are stored only on your device (in your browser's IndexedDB). A mark showing whether you have seen the opening film is also kept only on your device (in localStorage), so that it does not play again. Life-record images you drop are not stored. We cannot see any of this.
privacy.play3: How to delete: open a card and press the button that removes it to delete that one card, press the button that clears the catalogue to delete them all, or delete this site's data in your browser settings.
privacy.play5: About AI: neither your images nor the contents of your cards are sent to any AI (on 25 October 2026 we removed the option that let the AI read the text on a life record, and the feature where the AI wrote a name and story when spirits were bound). AI is used only once a night, when you enter the last room in Light the Night Museum (item 7 below). At that moment, the numbers (file names) of the artworks of that night's spirits, the spirits' names and the page language are sent to our relay server (Cloudflare Workers). The relay server adds the artwork titles and backgrounds we prepared and the artwork images (CC0 works released by the museums and hosted on our site), sends them to the API of OpenAI (USA), and the AI writes that night's story (a title and captions) and a plan for the music. The guardian (human card), life records and key images are never sent. The API key is provided by us; you do not need to enter one. The relay server stores neither what is sent to the AI nor its answer. To keep our costs within a fixed range, we use OpenAI's free allowance, which is given on the condition that OpenAI may use what is sent to improve its AI. This means OpenAI may use what is sent (including the spirits' names) to improve its AI. To prevent overuse, the relay server counts only the amount used that day and the number of requests per mark made from shortened, irreversible connection information, and deletes them the next day.
privacy.play6: Analytics: as on other pages, page views are counted with Google Analytics (section 12). In addition, only the counts of spirits awakened, bindings, bonds and children are sent. Images, names and card contents are never sent.
privacy.play7: Light the Night Museum (dropper-tools.com/en/play/night.html; it replaced Battle in October 2026): it only reads the cards in your catalogue on your device (it does not change them). Card contents are not sent anywhere, except the spirits' names and artwork numbers sent to the AI when you enter the last room ("About AI" above). When you drop a life-record image as the key to the last door, this page opens the catalogue page in a hidden frame, hands it the image, recognises it on your device and makes a Guardian (human card) for that night only (the Guardian is not added to your catalogue and is used only for that night's last room; the image is not sent anywhere or saved). The key images for doors 2 to 4 (a Silk picture, a Hubble photo, a TheSkyLive star map) are only recognised on your device by their shapes and colours (and, for the Hubble photo, its file name); they are not sent to any AI or to us, and are not saved. The number of nights you played (how many times you reached Dawn or a Quiet Morning), the frames you received in the morning, and a copy of each framed spirit (its name, rarity, small card picture, description, and the title and story of the museum artwork it was born from, so it stays in the last corridor even if you empty your catalogue) are kept only on your device (in your browser's localStorage). The catalogue page only reads which spirits are framed to mark them. Deleting this site's data in your browser settings removes them. The 20-second video of the last room and the walk down the last corridor are made on your device from that night's artwork images, the small pictures of your spirit cards, footage we prepared in advance and music synthesised on the spot. The video is not sent anywhere; it is saved to your device only when you press "Save the video". For analytics, only the counts of nights started, of last doors unlocked, of Dawns and Quiet Mornings reached and of spirits framed are sent.
privacy.ytBody: Some guide pages embed a YouTube video. The video loads from YouTube (Google) in privacy-enhanced mode (youtube-nocookie.com) only when you press the play button; nothing is sent to YouTube before that. After you press it, Google's privacy policy applies.
